# D-018 — Update DTOs and metamodels are generated, never hand-written

**Status:** accepted
**Invariant:** `rxcrud_gen.go` is generated output; a change to it must come from re-running `cmd/rxcrud`, and the generated file must be reproducible from the model source.

## The decision

`cmd/rxcrud` reads a package's Go source with `go/parser`, finds the structs that
carry `db` or `rel` tags (or are named with `-types`), and writes two things per
model into `rxcrud_gen.go`:

- `<Model>Update` — the partial-update DTO, `*T` for a non-nullable column and
  `crud.Opt[T]` for a nullable one ([[D-002]]);
- `<Model>Attrs` plus `var Model_ = specs.Metamodel[Model, ModelAttrs]()` — the
  typed metamodel, expanded through relations to `-depth` levels.

The file carries `// Code generated by rxcrud. DO NOT EDIT.` and is checked in.

## Why

**Why generated rather than reflective at run time.** The DTO could be a
`map[string]any` and the filter API could take strings. Both work and both move
the failure to a request: rename `CreatedAt` to `PublishedAt` and a hand-written
DTO still compiles, a string filter still compiles, and the break shows up as a
400 in production. Generated code breaks the build.

**Why generated rather than hand-written.** A DTO is mechanical — one field per
writable column, with the nullability rule from [[D-002]] applied. Hand-writing
it means the nullability decision is made by whoever is typing, per field, per
model, forever, and the wrong choice is silent: a `*T` where `Opt[T]` belongs
loses the ability to write NULL, and nobody notices until a client tries.

**Why source parsing rather than reflection over compiled types.** The generator
runs before the DTO exists, so it cannot import the package that will contain
it. `go/parser` also sees the type *as written* — `crud.Opt[int]`, `uuid.UUID`,
`time.Time` — which is what the output has to reproduce, and it lets the imports
be carried across (`generator.imports`).

**Why the flags exist.** Each one answers a case the default cannot.

| flag | the case |
| --- | --- |
| `-types User,Article` | ent's generated entities carry no `db` tags, so nothing marks them as models. Naming them explicitly is what makes an untagged foreign struct a model. |
| `-import` + `-into` | write the output into *your* package instead of the ORM's. `UserUpdate` would collide with ent's own update builder, and `ent generate` owns that directory and would delete or overwrite the file. `-into` without `-import` is refused, because the generated file could then not name the model types. |
| `-readonly CreatedAt` | a server-owned column: still filterable, sortable and present in the metamodel, but out of the update DTO. The same effect as `db:",immutable"` for a struct you do not own and cannot tag. |
| a `version` / `lock` column | left out of the DTO and kept in the metamodel, without a flag. The repository advances the lock, and `crud.PlanFor` refuses a DTO that names it — so this is not a preference, it is the only shape that declares. |
| `-skip Internal` | drop the field entirely, like `db:"-"`. For a column the API should not know about at all — it leaves the metamodel too, so it is not filterable either. That is the difference from `-readonly` and it is the reason both exist. |
| `-depth` | relation expansion is a tree and a cyclic schema is infinite. Default 2. |
| `-no-dto` / `-no-meta` | generate one half. |

**Why embedded structs are flattened.** The runtime flattens them
(`crud/meta.go:collectFields`), so the generator has to as well or `gorm.Model`
would silently take `ID` and the timestamps out of the metamodel — the fields
would exist at run time and be missing at compile time.
`wellKnownEmbeds` covers `gorm.Model`, whose fields the parser cannot read
because they live in another package.

**Why a struct-typed field from the same package is skipped.** It is a relation
holder or somebody else's bookkeeping, never a column. That is what keeps ent's
`Edges UserEdges` out of the DTO, and it mirrors the runtime rule.

## What it forbids

- Do not hand-edit `rxcrud_gen.go`. The `DO NOT EDIT` header is not decorative;
  `TestGeneratedFileIsUpToDate` and `TestTheGeneratedStoresAreUpToDate`
  regenerate and compare.
- Do not make the generator's output depend on map iteration order. See
  [[D-014]] — model names and imports are sorted, and the up-to-date tests only
  work because of it.
- Do not merge `-skip` and `-readonly` into one flag. They differ in whether the
  field survives in the metamodel, which is the difference between "not
  writable" and "not addressable".
- Do not write into the ORM's own directory. `-into` exists because that
  directory is owned by the ORM's generator.
- Do not add a field to a generated DTO by hand instead of tagging the model.

## Where it lives

- `cmd/rxcrud/main.go` — the package doc lists every flag with its reason.
- `cmd/rxcrud/main.go:generator.load` — parses the directory, two passes: struct
  names first so a field whose type is a local struct is recognised as a
  relation holder rather than a column.
- `cmd/rxcrud/main.go:generator.parseModel` — tag reading, the `-types` override,
  the skip rules.
- `cmd/rxcrud/main.go:dtoType` — the `*T` / `crud.Opt[T]` decision.
- `cmd/rxcrud/main.go:attrType` — `Str` / `Ord` / `Cmp` / `Attr`.
- `cmd/rxcrud/main.go:wellKnownEmbeds` — `gorm.Model`.
- `cmd/rxcrud/main.go:generator.embedded` — local embeds via the parser, foreign
  ones via the table above.
- `cmd/rxcrud/render.go:generator.render` — the output, including the sorted
  import block.
- `cmd/rxcrud/render.go:generator.renderAttrs` — relation expansion with the
  depth bound and a cycle guard.
- `Makefile:generate` — regenerates the library's own examples and both test
  stores.
- `example/blog/rxcrud_gen.go`, `test/entstore/rxcrud_gen.go`,
  `test/gormstore/rxcrud_gen.go` — the checked-in outputs.

## Proven by

- `TestGeneratedFileIsUpToDate` in `example/blog/blog_test.go` and
  `TestTheGeneratedStoresAreUpToDate` in `test/integration/codegen_test.go` —
  regenerate and diff. These are what make the checked-in files trustworthy.
- `TestGeneratedCodeCompilesAndValidates` in `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go` — the
  output is not just text; it compiles and the resulting DTO validates against
  the model's schema.
- `TestOutputIsByteIdenticalAcrossRuns` in `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go`.
- `TestGeneratedDTOTypesFollowNullability` in `example/blog/blog_test.go` and
  `TestUpdateDTOFollowsNullability` in `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go`.
- `TestUpdateDTOLeavesOutWhatCannotBeWritten` in `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go`.
- `TestReadonlyKeepsAFieldQueryableButNotWritable` and
  `TestSkipRemovesAFieldEverywhere` in `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go` — the pair that
  pins the difference between the two flags. The `-readonly` test asserts the
  field is *still in the metamodel*, which is the half that would otherwise rot.
- `TestIntoAnotherPackageQualifiesTheModelTypes`,
  `TestIntoAnExistingPackageKeepsItsName` and `TestIntoWithoutImportIsRefused` in
  `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go`.
- `TestEmbeddedStructsAreFlattened` and
  `TestGormModelIsFlattenedFromTheWellKnownTable` in `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go`.
- `TestRelationsBecomeNestedAttributeStructs` and
  `TestDepthBoundsHowFarRelationsExpand` in `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go`.
- `TestGeneratingOnlyOneHalf` and `TestAPackageWithNothingToGenerateIsAnError` in
  `cmd/rxcrud/gen_test.go`.
- `TestEntGeneratedMetamodel` in `test/integration/ent_model_test.go` — the
  `-types` case against ent's real generated entity.
